idiom: He told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.
I've sent the proposal, so the ball is in your court now.
I hate going to the dentist, but I just need to bite the bullet.
We've been working for ten hours straight. Let's call it a day.
робити щось дешевше/швидше на шкоду якості
If we start cutting corners, our clients will notice the drop in quality.
The party got totally out of hand, and the police showed up.
give someone the benefit of the doubt
повірити на слово / не підозрювати у злогомірі
I'll give her the benefit of the doubt and assume she missed the email.
hit the nail on the head
You hit the nail on the head with your analysis of the market.
We're all worried about layoffs; we're in the same boat.
Keep your chin up, things will get better soon.
let the cat out of the bag
We wanted the party to be a surprise, but John let the cat out of the bag.
If you don't apply now, you might miss the boat.
The exam was a piece of cake; I finished it in 20 minutes.
Are you serious or just pulling my leg?
We don't always see eye to eye on project priorities.
про легку руку / про кого згадали, той і з'явився
Hi Sarah, speak of the devil! We were just talking about your report.
перехопити ініціативу / забрати всю славу собі
I didn't want to announce my news at your party and steal your thunder.
take with a grain of salt
ставитися скептично / не вірити на всі 100%
Take his advice with a grain of salt; he doesn't know the whole story.
I'm feeling a bit under the weather today, so I'll work from home.
I have an exam tomorrow, so I'll be burning the midnight oil tonight.
slang: Please send me the report ASAP.
кінець дня (часто плутають із загальним заходом сонця)
I need this presentation by EOD.
у разі якщо я зробив це мій
ICYMI, here is the link to the new policy.
IMO, we should postpone the meeting.
TBH, I didn't understand the instructions.
для вашої інформації (може звучить занадто сухо)
FYI, the coffee machine is broken.
What is your ETA for the project?
AFAIK, the office is closed tomorrow.
TL;DR: we exceeded our sales target.
I am OOO until next Monday.
The venue for the party is TBD.
Don't worry about the late reply, NBD.
Btw, are you coming to the lunch?
WDYM? The file is right here.
LMK if you need any help.
I went to the party just because of FOMO.
prov: Actions speak louder than words.
Не слова красять людину, а діла.
Дії говорять голосніше за слова.
He promised to help us move, but he never showed up. Actions speak louder than words.
All that glitters is not gold.
Не все те золото, що блищить.
That cheap designer bag fell apart after a week. All that glitters is not gold.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
Краще синиця в руках, ніж журавель у небі.
Птах у руці коштує двох у кущі.
I could wait for a higher salary offer, but I'll take this secure job now. A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
Невбитого ведмедя шкуру не ділять (або: Циплят восени рахують).
Не рахуй своїх курчат до того, як вони вилупляться.
Don't spend the prize money yet; you haven't won the competition. Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
Every cloud has a silver lining.
Немає лиха без добра.
Кожна хмара має срібну підкладку.
Losing my job forced me to start my own business. Every cloud has a silver lining.
Bite off more than you can chew.
Набрати забагато зобов'язань (або: Не по соломі сани).
Вкусити більше, ніж можеш прожувати.
By taking on three extra projects, she bit off more than she could chew.
Blessing in disguise.
Лихо не без добра.
Благословення в маскарадному костюмі.
Missing my flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise because I met my future business partner at the terminal.
Break the ice.
Розтопити кригу (зробити перший крок у знайомстві).
Зламати кригу.
He told a funny joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.
Call a spade a spade.
Називати речі своїми іменами.
Назвати лопату лопатою.
Let's stop beating around the bush and call a spade a spade: our project is failing.
Cry over spilled milk.
Після бою кулаками не махають (або: Плакати над розлитим молоком).
We lost the game, but there's no use crying over spilled milk. We must practice harder.
Curiosity killed the cat.
Допитливість до добра не доводить.
Сקרава вбила кота.
Don't ask him about his surprise gift; curiosity killed the cat.
Cut corners.
Робити щось халтурно (або: Спускати на гальмах).
Різати кути.
If you cut corners on building the foundation, the house won't be safe.
Devil's advocate.
Адвокат диявола (опонувати заради істини).
I don't really disagree with the plan, but I'll play devil's advocate to test its flaws.
Easy come, easy go.
Як прийшло, так і пішло.
Легко прийшло, легко пішло.
He spent all his lottery winnings in a week. Easy come, easy go.
Get out of hand.
Вийти з-під контролю.
Вийти з руки.
The children's party got completely out of hand when the cake was smashed.
Give someone the benefit of the doubt.
Повірити на слово (або: Ухвалити сумнів на користь обвинуваченого).
Дати комусь перевагу сумніву.
I didn't have proof he lied, so I gave him the benefit of the doubt.
Hit the nail on the head.
Влучити в саму точку.
Вбити цвях у голову.
You hit the nail on the head with your analysis of our marketing problem.
In the heat of the moment.
У гарячці (під впливом сильних емоцій).
У спеці моменту.
He said some hurtful things in the heat of the moment, but he later apologized.
Kill two birds with one stone.
Вбити двох зайців одним пострілом.
Вбити двох птахів одним каменем.
By walking to the grocery store, I got some exercise and bought dinner—killing two birds with one stone.
Let sleeping dogs lie.
Не буди лихо, поки воно тихо.
Дозволь сплячим собакам лежати.
I know you want to bring up the old argument, but it's better to let sleeping dogs lie.
